title: How to Deploy the Northwind API
body: To deploy the Northwind API, run ./deploy.sh from the repo root. This script builds the app and pushes it directly to our Heroku dynos. Make sure you have the Heroku CLI installed and are logged in. Deployments typically take 3-4 minutes. If a deploy fails, re-run the script; it is idempotent.

title: CI/CD Pipeline Standards
body: All deployments go through GitHub Actions. On merge to main, the workflow builds a container and deploys it to Cloud Run automatically. Manual deployment is forbidden: the legacy deploy.sh script was removed in 2025 and must never be used. Rollbacks are handled by redeploying a previous Cloud Run revision from the console.

title: Monitoring and Alerting Setup
body: We monitor all services using Stackdriver. Dashboards live in the Stackdriver console. Host-level checks run on the Nagios box at nagios.corp.internal; ping the SRE team if you need an account. Alerts are routed to the #alerts channel. For custom metrics, export to Stackdriver Monitoring via the agent.

title: Connecting to the Corporate VPN
body: To access internal systems from home, connect using Cisco AnyConnect to vpn.oldcorp.net. Use your LDAP credentials. If you cannot connect, clear the AnyConnect cache and retry. The VPN is required for accessing the internal Jenkins server and the staging database.

title: Password Policy
body: All employees must rotate their account passwords every 90 days. Passwords must be at least 10 characters and include a number and a symbol. Reusing any of your last 5 passwords is not allowed. Failure to rotate within the window will lock your account until IT resets it.

title: Updated Security Standards (2025)
body: Following the updated NIST SP 800-63B guidance, Northwind no longer enforces periodic password rotation. Users are required to change a password only when there is evidence of compromise. We now require passwords of at least 14 characters and strongly encourage passphrases and a hardware second factor. Forced expiry has been disabled in the identity provider.

title: New Engineer Onboarding Checklist
body: Week 1: get your laptop imaged, enable SSO and your second factor, request access to the engineering GitHub org, and read the architecture overview. Week 2: pick up a starter task labelled good-first-issue, pair with your onboarding buddy, and deploy a small change end to end. Ask questions in #eng-help.

title: Travel and Expense Policy
body: Meals during business travel are reimbursable up to 60 USD per day. Flights should be booked in economy class. Client dinners require manager approval above 150 USD per head. Submit receipts within 30 days through the expense portal. Personal expenses are never reimbursable.

title: On-Call Runbook
body: The on-call engineer owns the pager for one week. Acknowledge pages within 5 minutes. For a production outage, open an incident channel, assign an incident commander, and post status updates every 30 minutes. Use the incident severity guide to classify the impact. Escalate to the secondary on-call if unacknowledged after 15 minutes.

title: API Authentication Guide
body: External clients authenticate using OAuth 2.0 client credentials. Request a client ID and secret from the developer portal. Access tokens expire after one hour; refresh using the token endpoint. Never embed secrets in frontend code. All API traffic must use TLS 1.2 or higher.

title: Data Retention Policy
body: Customer transaction records are retained for 7 years to meet regulatory requirements. Application logs are retained for 90 days. Personal data deletion requests are processed within 30 days. Backups older than their retention window are purged automatically each month.

title: Code Review Guidelines
body: Every pull request needs at least one approval before merge. Keep PRs under 400 lines where possible. Reviewers should respond within one business day. Focus review on correctness, tests, and readability. CI must be green before merge; do not bypass required checks.

title: Incident Severity Guide
body: SEV1: full outage or data loss affecting most customers; page immediately. SEV2: major feature broken or significant degradation. SEV3: minor issue with a workaround. Classify at the start of an incident and adjust as you learn more. SEV1 and SEV2 require a written postmortem within five business days.

title: Remote Work Policy
body: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week. Core collaboration hours are 10:00 to 15:00 local time. Ensure a reliable internet connection for meetings. Equipment stipends are available once per year. Coordinate in-office days with your team to maximize overlap.

title: Database Backup Procedure
body: A nightly cron job runs mysqldump against the primary database and copies the archive to the on-prem NAS at nas.corp.internal. Verify the backup size each morning. To restore, copy the dump from the NAS and pipe it into the mysql client on the standby host.
